_comment: The job domain's criteria — the rulings of 2026-09-13 in docs/plans/job-domain.plan.md. Every rule here is movable: the one eligibility rule is a switch, and nothing is a non-overridable set. Patterns are regex fragments applied with ~…~u to FOLDED text (lowercase, accents stripped, U+00A0 as a space). A gitignored criteria.local.json beside this file overrides field by field. Unknown keys are refused.
_role_words: H5 — the MANDATORY filter is a TITLE role gate: a title that was read and matches none of these is rejected; an empty title never is. Stems where French inflects (`developpeu` covers développeur, développeuse, développeur.euse, développeur(se)), because a gate that misses a feminine or inclusive form rejects a real offer in silence. Every one of the 57 distinct titles in the 20 LinkedIn captures passes (JobCriteriaTest). An EMPTY list is refused at load.
_title_rejects: H6, plus H4's business-developer family — title words that REJECT even though the role gate passed (`Business Developer` contains `developer`, `Data Engineer` contains `engineer`). The first label that fires names the rejection. DevOps is deliberately absent: a developer role asking for some DevOps is wanted (ruled). `apprentissage automatique` is machine learning, so it is a DATA reject and never an alternance one.
_exclude_patterns: H4 — the developer's own extra exclusions over title AND description. Empty on purpose: the ruled rejects are above, and this is the ordinary user list.
_contracts: H3 — a STATED contract set made ONLY of these rejects. CDI, freelance and portage are the ruled scope; a dual offer is a set, and one ruled contract keeps it. Intérim, VIE and contractuel are not listed (N5: shown, not rejected). Only the classifier's canonical words may appear here.
_pay: H1/H2 and the pay component. REJECTED only when a STATED gross salary's upper bound (13 months for a monthly figure) is under the salary floor, or a stated TJM's upper bound is under the TJM floor — and on a dual offer only when EVERY stated line is under its floor (N2). Never on unknown pay, a net figure, a package (N1) or a portage salary (N6). Scored from the floor (0) to the target (full share) on the upper bound.
_eligibility: H7 (N3) — one switch. While false, an offer STATING French nationality or a defence clearance as required is rejected (negation read first). The developer flips it after naturalisation.
_location: H8 (N4) — rejected only when the place is stated OUTSIDE Île-de-France AND on-site or hybrid work is stated. LinkedIn gives no postcode, so places are recognised by NAME. A place matching neither list is UNKNOWN and never rejects; a bare `France` is unknown. Outside wins a collision (`Saint-Denis, La Réunion`). Read on the listing's location field only — a head office named in a description is not the job's place.
_stack: Multi-stack and GROUPED (ruled). A BACK term earns the back share; with no back term, an ADJACENT term earns the adjacent share (half of back); a FRONT term adds the front share. back + front = 1. With none of those, an OTHER primary stack is named and earns 0; with no stack word at all the component is unknown and says so. Never a reject. Boundary traps are pinned by JobCriteriaTest: Java vs JavaScript, `vue` the French word, `go` as gigaoctet, Scala vs scalable, .NET vs internet, React vs réactivité, TS inside words.
_green: GREEN signals (ruled): each GROUP that fires earns an equal part of the green share, a group counts once however many of its terms fire, and every term is read NEGATION FIRST. Legacy modernisation sits in craft. `ai` is the tool sense only — AI as a way of writing code, never an AI product. `bdd` is deliberately absent: in French it is a database.
_red: RED signals (ruled): run-only work. Each term that fires takes `penalty` points off the total, capped at `cap` — outside the 100, so the weights still sum to 100. A RED signal names itself on the push and NEVER hides an offer. Negation first: `pas d'astreinte` is not an astreinte.
_remote: Remote & work conditions, one component. The share follows the stated remote days per week; a hybrid offer that states no days earns `hybrid_unstated_share` [Speculative — the LinkedIn card says `Hybride` and nothing more on 69 of 115 cards, so this number decides most of them; re-measure after a week]. An UNSTATED mode is unknown and says so — never read as on site. A work condition adds `conditions_bonus`, clamped at the full share. Conditions are read negation first.
_level: Title level shares (research C7, speculative until measured). An unlabelled title is a real reading — it states no level — so it earns a middle share rather than `hors score`.
_freshness: Full share up to `peak_days` since publication, 0 at twice it. A LinkedIn card carries no publication date, so on that source the component is always unknown and says so — the weights are NOT rebalanced for it.
_weights: Ruled 2026-09-13 15:37 — sum to 100, re-measured after a week of real rows. RED is outside the 100.
